en: Preface to the Five Patriarchs, Year of the Ox (Bichou).
During the summer retreat at the Wanfeng Pass of Sheng’en Chan Monastery, four senior monks—Minji, Zhengche, and two others—attended the pass.
One day, they all adjusted their robes, prostrated themselves, and requested: "We have heard from various quarters..."
Venerable Master, you wish to erase the tenets of the five houses and transmit solely the single matter of Śākyamuni’s holding up the flower, calling this "directly pointing to the ultimate.
Yet, you do not know whether the establishment of these five schools was indeed erroneous. I pray that you will grant me a word on this.
He resolved their difficulties by saying to Mi: "One who commands an army must possess the military tally; one who awakens to the mind must transmit the Dharma-seal.
If the tally does not match, it is deemed treachery and falsehood; if the Dharma is not identical, it is deemed a heterodox path. Since the time of Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja..."
There is not a single word or a single dharma that is not a seal of the essential tenets of the Five Houses. Those of antiquity realized this;
they thus silently accorded with its subtlety without making distinctions. Later followers emulated them, and so established their own sects to prevent forgery.

Those who would erase the Five Houses in an attempt to transmit the Dharma as a solitary lineage are merely the ringleaders of those who break seals and melt down tokens for their own convenience. How could they possibly be the [true heirs] of the Five...?
"Is he not a loyal minister of our school and a Dharma general of the Seven Buddhas? Alas! That the Dharma is perishing and that gods and humans are filled with anxiety is precisely because of this.
How can one not stand in awe? One might ask: 'In the past, there were those who burned incense and scorched their crowns to secretly transmit the essential tenets;
yet Dahui exposed them all at once on his placard to shatter such fox-like arts. If that is so, what is so precious about the essential tenets of today? To this, we reply:"
What they transmit is merely a clandestine seizing of symbols and a feigned reliance on faith.

As for the principle that "each dharma is self-evident" and "mind and mind seal one another," how could it be like the secret transmission within a room to those who are but "dead sons of the Dharma"? Indeed, those who claim to transmit the fundamental tenets have not awakened to the fundamental tenets;
those who smear over the fundamental tenets do not know the fundamental tenets. Herein, one must grasp and uphold that which has not yet been broken.
The Secret Seal (Mudrā) is used to capture and entrust the treacherous faction of the false. This administration is for the true sons who now shoulder the life-vein of the Tathāgata;
how could those who are frivolous and excessive be allowed to mingle therein? Thus, the five schools were originally traced back and entrusted to four sons.
The sons bowed their heads in gratitude and each vowed to strictly uphold the seal of authority so that the true transmission might endure forever.
Preface by the Mili Family, Spring of the Wuchen Year of the Chongzhen Era.
*The Source of the Five Schools* composed by the Śramaṇa Fǎzàng of Wànfēng.
Disciple Sanxue Shangli has read the records of the Linji school and once saw a painter’s depiction of the seven buddhas.
It begins with Vipaśyin Buddha (Viyinwang Fo), which is represented merely as a large circle.
Following the Perfect Circle (Yuanxiang), each of the Seven Buddhas has their own verbal expression (*yanquan*).

Although these expressions differ, the essential meaning of the Buddhas' verses does not transcend the Perfect Circle. Now, "Majesty" (*wei*) refers to that which lies beyond form; "Sound" (*yin*) refers to that which lies beyond voice.
"King of Majestic Sound" (*Weiyinwang*) exists beyond both form and sound; it has never been recorded in writing, and there is no basis for verification through characters or words.
This is the most supreme matter of the past. If one looks upward to what was manifested by Nāgārjuna, it is the so-called signless samādhi;

this refers to the period prior to Dīpaṃkara. The circular symbols (yuanxiang) originated with the various patriarchs of India, while the verses of the Seven Buddhas were transmitted from Bodhidharma;
thus, they both have their origins. Let us examine this: the circular symbols already embody the essential tenets of the Five Houses.
Thus it is. Each of the five houses has emerged from its own perspective, yet there is a primary orthodox lineage.

First, the fundamental principle of Linji appeared; this was cast forth directly, severing the life-root of men. Within the "one zero" (the absolute), guest and host roll on together, entering straight into the eye of Śiva.
As it is said: "How can one ask about the ceaseless following of the current? When true illumination is boundless, explain it to him. Departing...

"Mutual separation is called 'the person not receiving it'; once the 'whisker-cutting blade' has been used, one must immediately polish it. Next is Yunmen’s "Three Phrases" and the "Single-Word Barrier.
The "Circular Diagrams" (yuanxiang) of the Guiyang and Linji schools are fundamentally based on this.

Fayen discussed the meaning of the teachings beyond the "Six Phases," while Caodong distinguished "reciprocity" (huixu) at the intersection of black and white. Within this single circle (○), all five schools are fully present.
Furthermore, as the principles branching out from this reach their ultimate limit, there is nothing among the profound, mysterious, deep, and subtle teachings that is not fully contained herein.
Thus, each of the Seven Buddhas summarized [the Dharma] with a single verse. The verse of Vipaśyin Buddha says: "The body receives birth from within the formless;
It is like illusions manifesting various forms. The mind-consciousness of the illusory person is originally non-existent; Both sin and merit are empty and void."
As for their respective abodes: to possess marks while being without marks is the Linji school—direct, decisive, and incisive.
To subtly reveal its essential meaning therein is the Yunmen school. To receive the perfect circle within the state of no-marks is what is called the Guiyang school.

The meaning of the six aspects of the formless body is what is called the Dharma-Eye school (Hōgen-shū). The body being simultaneously formless is the essential principle of the Cao-Dong five ranks (Go-i).
All others—the six Buddhas and the various patriarchs of the four and seven generations—are no different from this; it is simply that they have not explicitly clarified and revealed it.
This is why the prophecy of Prajñātāra says: "Two young cassia trees shall flourish for a long time. This is the "tongs" (kemma).
The record of the division into five schools begins with the two patriarchs. Thus, Nanyue and Qingyuan are regarded as the sources of the five schools.
It is further said: "In China, the path is not wide; there are no divergent ways. One must simply cause one's descendants to walk upon their own feet.

When the golden rooster understands how to hold a single grain of millet in its beak, it shall offer it to the Arhat monks of the ten directions. This record was intended for someone surnamed Ma to produce.
Among the ten schools, there are two that constitute the orthodox lineage. From their foundations, four schools shall emerge, yet only the Linji school is the true, direct transmission.
When the First Patriarch arrived at Jinling, Emperor Wu asked, "Is there merit in building monasteries and ordaining monks?
The Patriarch replied, "In truth, there is no merit. This was the direct and unadorned speech of Linji. Yunmen, Fayan, and Muzhou...

[The Master] looked up. What is there that he does not possess? The Emperor asked, "Why do you have no merit? The Patriarch said, "This is merely a small fruit of humans and devas, a cause of outflows (*sāsrava*).
It follows the form like a shadow; though it exists, it is not real. Is this not the language of Cao-Dong?

When the Second Patriarch arrived, a layman requested to repent for his sins. The Patriarch said, "Bring forth your sin, and I shall repent it for you. After a long while, the layman said, "I cannot find it..."
"Sin is ultimately unobtainable. The Patriarch said, "I have finished repenting for your sin for you. Bring forth the sin; once it is brought forth, the repentance is complete.
This is the Linji and Yunmen school. The questions and answers are clear and distinct. The cases of Muzhou and Yangshan belong to the Guiyang, Fayan, Caodong, and Linji schools.
A śrāmaṇera asked the Third Patriarch for the Dharma-gate of liberation. The Patriarch said, "Who has bound you? This is not of the Linji or Yunmen school.
The man who planted pine trees asked the Fourth Patriarch, "May I hear the Way of the Dharma? The Patriarch said, "You are already old;
even if you were to hear it, would you be able to transform others extensively? If you were to come again, I would still wait for you. One must fully contemplate these words.

Thus, Linji and Yunmen subtly open and close [the gates of teaching], and therein all the various schools are fully contained. When the Fifth Patriarch received Lu (Huineng), he struck the mortar with his staff three times;
was this not the laying of the foundation for Linji? When the Sixth Patriarch asked Nanyue, "Where have you come from? he replied, "From Mount Song.
The Patriarch said, "What kind of thing is it that comes like this? He replied, "To describe it as a single thing is not quite right."
The Patriarch asked, "Is there still cultivation and realization? [Dongshan] replied, "Cultivation and realization are not non-existent; however, defilement is not permitted.
Observe Master Xiangru’s statement, "To regard it as a thing is already incorrect. This is the principle of the Linji school, yet it is also the purport of Yunmen.
"Cultivation and realization are not non-existent; defilement is simply not permitted. Is this not the essential principle of the Dharma-eye of Miu and Yang?

Indeed, the source of the four schools originates here; the prophecy concerning the "Horse Colt" was settled here. When [Nanquan] went toward Master Ma to grind a tile, Master Ma asked, "What are you grinding the tile for?
He replied, "To make a mirror. Master Ma said, "How can grinding a tile produce a mirror? He replied, "To sit [in meditation]."
"How could Chan possibly achieve Buddhahood?"—this single phrase alone caused the fundamental tenets of Linji to flourish greatly; Yunmen likewise possessed this.
When asked, "What is it that is such? he replied, "It is like an ox pulling a cart. If the cart does not move, beating the ox is precisely what one must do."
"Striking is precisely it. Thus, the Dharma-eye of Guishan and Yangshan began here. Mazu said: "The head of the storehouse is white;
the head of the sea is black. Sun-face Buddha, Moon-face Buddha. Sometimes he shouted; sometimes he struck. This is the Linji school.
During a monk’s visit, the Master drew a circle and said: "I strike if you enter; I strike if you do not enter. As soon as the monk entered, the Master struck him.
The monk said, "Master, you may not strike me. The Master leaned on his staff and desisted.
This single case alone encompasses all four schools of Chan. He let out a thunderous shout after hanging his whisk at Baizhang;
for three days he was deaf before Huangbo’s tongue-lashing. After the three painful blows, the great tree shaded the heavens, and the Linji school rose high.
Yet, regarding the pinnacle of the Five Houses: from Vīradhvaja to the present day, the cream within the milk is most refined and most wondrous.
Is it not here that "the colt tramples the people of the world"? One thus knows that the three punches beneath the ribs of Dayú (Dàgū) were precisely intended for this.
Closing the secret and opening the manifest; dividing horizontally and binding vertically. Treading alone upon the four houses and emerging from the three phrases to encompass all.

The four "Discriminations of Conditions" exhaustively strip away the great framework of person, environment, and dharmas; the three "Essentials of the Mysteries" roll back the gates of birth and death to return them to the summit.

Only when the subtle divisions of the Way and Dharma are mastered can one begin to realize that phenomena, mind, and Buddha are each and every thing; only when the two and the three are identical can one truly proceed.
Every word cuts through the profound. When the shadowed grass stirs, the master is within himself, testing others; when the *vajra* is raised, the power is in his wrist, shattering things.
The Master occupies a ground where those who drift aimlessly do not recognize the origin of his coming. A shout has no source from which it arises;

those who take it as something real will surely be lost in confusion regarding its point of descent. With a single shout in both halls, Lu Xun was bewildered by the Eight-Array formation; in two places he yielded.
The Guest: Zhuge Liang possessed the strategy of hiding among the reeds. The second Zen guest and host reach completion upon ascending the seat.
The fourth guest-host dynamic employs a function as lethal as a pit of glue. Sometimes a student shouts first to provoke the spearhead; one must guard against hidden soldiers.
Sometimes a master of knowledge seizes the initiative to raid the ranks; it is vital to lay down traps. Sometimes the husband sings and the wife follows; sometimes they divide the borders.

Carving out territory, they share a single scene of shameless folly. Releasing and gathering, taking and giving, they intermingle. Filling their bags with sand and reducing the number of cooking fires, each looks only to their own success.
They bind themselves in feigned surrender, yet alone administer a cold, hidden sting. Whispering and murmuring like hidden vipers; thundering and crashing like foxes wetting their tails.
They employ the Mohe sword after the era of Great Peace has passed; they hold up the ancestral seal in a heaven that is not yet settled.
Lifting one’s head toward the heavens—“Who is this person? Hanging a mirror before the window—how can demons or heterodoxies be tolerated? One must wait for the mind to die in order to suppress it;
one must urgently employ the illumination of what precedes. First capture the “lower” and depart from it; briefly pick up and employ the lamp that follows.
He ferries those in need across the waters of the Black Wind Ghost Kingdom; he brings forth clear skies beyond the realm where blue waves resound in song.

At every turn, he seeks that which transcends the ordinary; at every step, he strives to master the initiative before the opportune moment. Those who have realized the Dharma exhaust the Dharma itself, leaving no further "people" (phenomena) behind.

The deceased person administers medicine according to the individual. Striking the strings of the *siṃha* lute, all other sounds are silenced; dripping lion’s milk, it causes the donkey’s curd to burst apart.
Having passed through this point, one dwells in ease wherever one is. Like moving clouds and falling rain, they do not dampen the immortal’s robe.
To drive off lightning and thunder—is this not due to the wrath of Heaven? Xinghua attained realization upon receiving a single blow while wearing his worn-out patchwork robe;
he hid himself within an ancient temple, which led Kebin to be further fined and expelled after being struck with a staff.

Nan-yuan brought up the principle of "the simultaneous moment of pecking and hatching," yet when he missed the mark, he struck him anyway, ultimately causing that monk to see the lamp at the very moment the staff broke.

Moving within the shadows, Fengxue entered the Dharma-gate of the Mysterious and the Essential while under the guidance of Shoukuo; thus, at Nan yuan’s place, the roles of guest and host were clearly defined.
Recognizing that the path of deception was not hungering for sustenance, he grasped the teacherless intent beneath the staff.
Fahua did not fall into silence upon the ancient road; at Baimiao’s place, the grass-robbers were utterly defeated. A true master does not seek to proclaim his own fame.

Jiantai saw through the strategy for "severing folly"; at Fenzhou, he saw that where the Elephant King walks, the tracks of foxes are severed, and thus he reached the place where one lets go of body and life.
Shishuang covered his mouth from behind, knowing that the Way transcends ordinary circumstances; he understood how to walk amidst the wild weeds.
Yangqi blocked the road and struck Ciming; knowing it was such a matter, he simply left it as it was and took his leave of Yunju to enter deep into the chaotic peaks.
Having already bowed after the two shouts, he then proceeded directly to the place of "shouldering the burden.

Old Huihui laughed and said, "Startled by Baiyun, once you have realized the point within this, you must let go and cast yourself down to the bottom of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff. At times he threw down his staff;
at other times he let one move pass. Wuzu Yan did not understand Xinghua’s words about the ancient temple, yet he understood Baiyun.
Yunyi gave a single shout, and the millstone immediately began to turn. Having escaped the body with a cold sweat, he spread far and wide a clear wind that carries on its back.

Zhaojue Qin exhausted the peripheral matters of the Five Patriarchs' functional mechanisms; because Master Yan refused to accept him, when he later took charge of Bazi, he again realized the "Cock's Crow.
Although he had mastered the single string that threads them all together, he still required a patch over his forehead and eyes added. Thus did Huqiu Long arrive and see him.
When he did not reach the point, [Zhaozhou] raised his fist. To explain this, one says: "Though the bamboo is dense, it does not hinder the flowing stream. In the end, he became a sleeping tiger.
Ying'an Hua laughed heartily when Zhaozhou set down the earthenware tray. To explain this, one says: "Where the power of Yu could not reach, the sound of the river flows toward the west."
"Only then will you see the true lion. Huazang Jie struck twice with his staff and then tossed it aside, saying, "Thirty years hence, you will have fully revealed your face.
Poban first struck once with his staff at the place where there is neither mind nor Buddha, briefly revealing a glimpse of the whole picture.

Wuzhun Fan said, "The three men have taken a tortoise and certified it as a soft-shelled turtle; truly, nothing is lacking. Xueyan Qin said: [Note: The provided text ends abruptly. The translation reflects the portion supplied.]

"Three fists and three prostrations" is the same as allowing the convergence of the Three Mysteries. Gao Feng Miaofeng treats it like a dragon's head and a snake's tail, rolling them all into one lump.
Zhongfeng Ben allows you half a share for "taking off the clothes once. Qianyan Chang saw a mouse eating a cat’s meal;
the bowl was broken, yet the shards remained. Wanfeng Wei saw a pure pitcher kicked over; the dull-witted fellow has already [finished his meal].
Thirty. Baozang Chi inherited the Three Essential Seals; his fangs and claws were not few. Dongming Xian relied on a renewed awakening;
in the end, nothing was left behind. Baofeng Xuan’s words were like drifting clouds; he had a path upon leaving his station. Tianqi Rui acted as a guest without yielding;
his departure had its own reason. Wumen Cong emerged from deep waters; fire burst forth from within the stone.
Xiaoyan Bao’s conduct combined both [the hard and the soft]. There was a dragon within the water; Huanyou transmitted a single point of lamp-flower, shattering the void.
Jinsu awakened through a single blow to the end, regardless of host or guest. Sanfeng Zang rescued the Great Dharma of Linji from seven hundred years ago;
its beginning and end remain intact. Soaring and concealing amidst the waters and clouds—where can one grasp it?
The two lineages converged into a single school, a development supported by historical precedent.
The Linji school reached its greatest flourishing under Fenyang Wuye and Ciming. From Ming, it passed to Yangqi, and from Huqiu...
From Zhen Xueyan Gaofeng, who presided over thousands of peaks and ten thousands of crags, until the time after Xiaoyan, the Dharma path was once again to be revitalized;
this has already been correctly detailed in the transmission lineage. Furthermore, under Shishuang, there appeared a monk from Biandou named Master Huanglong Nan.
When he had not yet attained awakening, he was inspired by Yunfeng Yue, who directed him to see Ciming. Ciming then asked:
Regarding the story of the Hermitess of Mount Tai: when he was unable to answer, Master Ming cursed him incessantly. The Master said, "Is cursing the compassionate bestowal of the Dharma?
Ming asked, "Do you understand this as a curse? At that, the Master realized the essential meaning.
Below him was Chan Master Bao Feng Zhen Jing Ke Wen, who went to see Huang Long but did not find resonance there. He then went to Xiangcheng and saw Master Shun. Shun asked, "What..."

[The Master] asked, "Where have you come from? [He] replied, "From Huanglong. [The Master] asked, "What words did Huanglong say? [He] replied, "Recently, the provincial government commissioned the Elder of Huangbo.

Huanglong gave this instruction: 'If someone can provide a phrase that accords with the truth when it is said, "One recites hymns on the bell tower while planting vegetables under the bed," they shall go to serve as the abbot.
At that time, the Senior Monk Sheng said, 'A fierce tiger sits in the middle of the road.'"
Long (Yuanlong) subsequently sent him to reside at Huangbo. Shun (Fushun) remarked unexpectedly, "If the Head Seat Sheng had only uttered a single turning word, he would have secured Huangbo's stay;
as for the Buddha-dharma, he has not even dreamed of it. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment regarding the application of Huanglong’s teaching.
Among those seated below was the Chan Master Qingliang Huihong Juefan. Wen frequently cited the words of Xuan Sha, "I have not yet reached the ultimate," to provoke doubt in him.
Whenever he offered a response, Wen would say, "Are you speaking of principles again? One day, he suddenly cast off his doubts and composed a verse, saying:
"Once Lingyun saw it, he did not see it again; On every branch, red and white, no flowers cling."
"I cannot bear those guests on fishing boats who come to the level ground to scoop up fish and shrimp. When Zhenjing saw this, he expressed his joy at it.

I once studied the principles of the Three Mysteries and attained a deep realization; however, when I sought to resolve my doubts by visiting various quarters, I found it difficult to find the right person.
Suddenly, I saw you, Master, composing the *Linji Zongzhi* and the section on Linji’s two head monks in the *Zhizheng Zhuan*.
The same shout—ancient and modern, mind-to-mind—is like a face-to-face seal. Furthermore, when examining his dharma heirs, there was none who continued the lineage.
Consequently, I vowed to succeed him remotely in his fundamental tenets, while the present dharma-lineage is transmitted after Xiangyan.
This is because I dare not fail the initiative of the *Gao Feng Lu* (Record of High Peak). Thus, I have herein set forth the orthodox pulse of Linji. And so...
I am single-mindedly devoted to this.
The Yunmen school,
since the one-character golden circle was cast forth by Weiyin, has followed the return of the brocade characters and verses of the Seven Buddhas to the Sixth Patriarch.
A bowl was passed down; it cannot be bitten or chewed whole. After Master Ma, this eye has been such that in shallow grass it is easy for reeds to grow tall.
When the Heavenly King offers a cake and Chongxin serves tea, one must see directly; any deliberation is a deviation.
When Deshan blew out the paper candle at Longtan, he truly cut off the flow. Xuefeng’s breast and mind overflow with this.
Emerging from Yantou, was this not like a box and its lid fitting together?

Thus, Shao Yang’s legs were momentarily broken within the door-slit of Muzhou, while he had long refined his understanding within the inner sanctum of Xuefeng, whereupon he declared: "Three catties of hemp; one bolt of cloth."
He thrusts the turtle’s nose into the Southern Mountain; he removes the iron shackles from the old man. He gasps with admiration at Master Lùquè; the *Sumeru* hūbǐng is just so.
As for the place where all Buddhas emerge: water flows upon the Eastern Mountain. The phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body: hiding one's body within the Northern Dipper.
Rice in the bowl, water in the bucket. Samādhi in every dust mote. Clouds over the Southern Mountain, North...
Mountain rain. The Buddha hands over the dew-pillar. He brings the three gates onto the lamp. He releases the honey-cake to make a steamed bun.
The sharp point of the sword [is found] within the eyebrows of the eight-fold *bōduò*. Thus there is the critical appraisal: "The red banner flashes. This is the lineage of Yunmen.
This is the source from which they emerge.
In the lineage of Miu and Yang, a single spark of fire blazes forth beyond the realm of non-duality; three times he shook the door-panel for those who are muddled regarding the two extremes.
In the interval between these, look at the water buffalo of Mount Gui; examine it beneath its waist. Dongping’s mirror is Mount Gui’s mirror; smash it with your hand.
Thus, both the ordinary and the holy are forgotten, and seeing and hearing are exhausted. When applied, one enters directly with a single blade;

when there is no thought, the spiritual flame is inexhaustible. Inserting the spade and pulling out the spade, dropping the feet and binding the feet—gaze downward and look upward within the gathering.
Let it go! It is not merely one, two, three, or four; yet the sword-blade is singular. Two mouths are tongueless, and ninety-six marks arise like clouds.
Father and son unite in their lineage; the single branch of Muzhou and Yangshan rises loftily.

The meaning of the Seven Buddhas’ Verses in the Dharma-Eye School (Hōgen-shū) is entirely the definitive language of the Sūtras; yet it clearly and independently reveals the essential tenets of Linji, Yunmen, and Miu-yang.
Only in the Cao-dong school is there the principle of "reciprocal interpenetration" (hu-hu), which manifests spontaneously without waiting for further explication or highlighting. Therefore:
The Dharma-eye school is entirely the ultimate pinnacle of the teaching school; it is the true moon of the teachings throughout the entire lifetime of the Buddha’s dispensation.

As for the transmission of Bodhidharma, there are such expressions as "if one seeks the mind, it is unattainable," "the bright mirror is not the stand," "this very mind is Buddha," and "neither mind nor Buddha.
Even when Tianwang heard Mazu’s words, he recognized that his own mind was originally Buddha.
It does not belong to gradual stages; it does not depend on cultivation or practice. Its essence is naturally suchness (*tathatā*); all myriad virtues are perfectly complete.
Enlightenment occurs in the very moment of speaking. When Longtan heard the words of Tianwang, he said: "Bring me the tea stand, and I will receive it for you.
Bring me the food, and I will accept it for you. When you bow, I simply lower my head. Where else could the essential point of the mind not be pointed out? The Master lowered his head.
The King said, "If I see it, I simply see it; if I try to conceive of it through thought, I immediately deviate. The Master asked, "How do you maintain this?
The King said, "I roam freely according to my nature and remain expansive and relaxed in accordance with conditions. I merely exhaust the ordinary mind; there is no separate 'sage-understanding'.
Deshan said, "To exhaust all profound dialectics is like placing a single hair in the great void; to exhaust all worldly mechanisms is like casting a single drop into a vast abyss. This...

This is precisely the fundamental source of Fayan’s Dharma-eye. At Yantou’s place, Xuefeng attained enlightenment, realizing that in the future, if he were to propagate the Great Teaching, it would flow forth one by one from his own breast, naturally covering heaven and earth.
Consequently, Xuansha emerged, who, based on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, elucidated the mind-ground; thus, his responses to circumstances became swift and agile, matching those of the *Sūtras*.

Yangshan and Daowei continued the tradition of Fengxue at Shoushan, returning once more to Huizhao. When Caodong reached Fushan, the tributary states returned to their sovereign.
Although Fayen entered the doctrinal schools, he could not escape the ultimate transformation. This alone is the one reality; the other two are... [omitted].
If that were so, it would not be true. Since the descendants of Linji have been entrusted with this great responsibility, how could they dare to betray their ancestral lineage?

To claim that "once awakened, all is finished and there is nothing more" is the talk of one who increases arrogance; to say "one blow of the hammer and it is accomplished, requiring no further effort" is the view of a shallow man.

You should know that great vessels are perfected late; do not abandon the path halfway through. The transmission of the teacher lies in the fundamental principle (*dharmapada*), not in mere names or titles. This is the source and flow.

Realization is the ultimate distinction. One may sit firmly in the fundamental state; yet those who seek mere exhilaration end up becoming arrogant, while those who are overly meticulous remain entangled to the very end.
Though there may still be a time for the entangled to be liberated, the arrogant ultimately stray onto a divergent path. I urge you most earnestly and instruct you in myriad ways:
do not sweep away the essential tenets to hide your own ineptitude; rather, it is precisely now that you must investigate the essence and exert yourself to the utmost.

When emotions are exhausted and eliminated in their subtlest forms, and when the person is forgotten and the Dharma extinguished, only then may one serve as a teacher and model for others, continuing the ancestral tradition of the Buddha.
Guard and maintain this well yourself, so that it shall not be severed.
The Commentary on the Dharma of Transmitting the Robe:
The World-Honored One went before the Many-Sons Stūpa and summoned Mahākāśyapa. He shared his seat with him and had him sit, then encircled him with his *saṃghāṭī* robe.
Thereupon, he declared: "I have secretly entrusted to you the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye. You must protect and uphold it. And...
The Buddha commanded Ānanda, "You shall be my successor in the transmission of the transformation; do not allow it to be severed. He then spoke this verse:

"The Dharma is fundamentally no-dharma; No-dharma and dharma are both dharma. Now, when I transmit no-dharma, How has dharma ever been dharma? At that time, after the World-Honored One had spoken this verse, he further addressed Kāśyapa:
"I shall take this golden-threaded *saṃghāṭī* robe and transmit it to you, so that you may turn [the wheel of the Dharma]."
He conferred upon him the status of a successor, saying: "Until the appearance of the Buddha Maitreya, do not allow this to decay.

When Kāśyapa heard these verses, he prostrated himself at [the Buddha's] feet and said: "Excellent, excellent! I shall follow these instructions, for I wish to remain respectful and obedient toward the Buddha.

Then the Venerable Haklena said to the Venerable Siṃha: "Our teacher has secretly made a prophetic prediction; it will not be long before we encounter hardship. The True Dharma-eye of the Tathāgata..."
The treasury: I shall now entrust it to you; you should protect it so that it may universally moisten all future generations. A verse says:

"When the correct teaching of knowledge and vision is given, both knowledge and vision are the mind. When the mind is present, there is knowledge and vision; knowledge and vision are right here and now.
After the Patriarch had spoken this verse, he secretly entrusted him with the *saṃghāṭī* robe. Upon reaching Master Bodhidharma, he said to Master Huike: "Internally transmitted is the Dharma-seal."

To verify the mind through realization, he externally bestowed the *kāṣāya* robe to establish the fundamental tenets. Yet, in later generations when people became degenerate, doubts vied with one another:
"I am a man from the Western Heaven; you are a native of this land. On what basis did you receive the Dharma? By what do you certify it?"

"You shall now receive this dharma of the robe. Hereafter, birth will become difficult; simply bring forth this robe along with my dharma verses to manifest [the teaching]. Your transformation of beings will be unhindered.
Two hundred years after my parinirvāṇa, the robe will cease to be transmitted, while the Dharma will pervade the entire realm of saṃsāra.

Those who clarify the Way will be many, but those who practice the Way will be few; those who expound the principle will be many, but those who penetrate the principle will be few. [They will] secretly accord and subtly harmonize..."

Those who have realized this number in the millions; you should propagate it. Do not disparage those who have not yet awakened. A single thought that turns back toward the source is identical to original attainment. Listen to my verse:
"I have come to this land from the beginning to transmit the Dharma and save the deluded masses. One flower blooms and five petals unfold."
The result was spontaneously accomplished. Later, when the Sixth Patriarch was striking the mortar at the command of the Fifth Patriarch, he entered the Patriarch’s chamber at night.
The Fifth Patriarch wrapped the patriarch in his *kāṣāya* so that no one would see him, and bestowed upon him the *kāṣāya* he had received, saying:
"Guard this well; do not let it be severed. Listen to my verse: 'When sentient beings come to sow seeds, the fruit arises from the ground. No... [text continues]
"Since emotion has no seed, it likewise has no nature and no arising. The Sixth Patriarch asked, "If the Dharma has now been received, to whom shall the robe be entrusted?
The Master replied, "In the past, when Bodhidharma first arrived, people did not yet believe him; therefore, he transmitted the robe to manifest that he had attained the Dharma.
Now that faith is already matured, the robe is merely a source of contention. It shall end with your person; it will no longer be transmitted. (At Mi) The commentary states:
Regarding the one who transmits the Dharma before the Bahuputra Stūpa, it was a prophetic declaration that the lineages of both the Patriarchs and the Buddhas would never be severed.
As for the World-Honored One sharing his seat with Kāśyapa, this demonstrates that the positions of Patriarch and Buddha are identical:

while the Buddha is in the world, the Buddha transmits the Dharma to the Patriarch; once the Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa, the Patriarch transmits the Dharma to the Buddha. This indicates that the Dharmakāya is what the Buddha values most.
Furthermore, the *saṃghāṭī* is used to encircle [the recipient] when conferring the Dharma; this signifies that the True Dharma takes the secret seal (*mudrā*) of the robe as its heart-seal.

Whenever there are points that are difficult to reach or difficult to believe, the robe and the Dharma are transmitted together. As for the "Treasury of the Eye of the True Dharma," it refers to the Dharma-eye transmitted from master to master.
The reason the "mind of nirvāṇa" is not mentioned is that the mind of self-awakening within each person is distinct [from the Dharma].
Each possesses its own inherent nature; it simply resides in the seal of the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, which is taken as the teacher’s dharma.
The command to Ānanda to act as his deputy means that through successive transmission of the teaching, there shall never be a lack of successors.

The four lines of the verse beginning "The Dharma is based on the Dharma, yet the Dharma is not a dharma" refer to the meaning of bestowing the characteristics of the dharma by pointing to the *kāṣāya*. Taking the golden-threaded *saṃghāṭī*...

"I entrust this robe to you to transmit to Maitreya Buddha, the one who succeeds me in his place. By first showing the robe, he demonstrated that the Dharma had been formally transmitted to the Patriarch;
by now delivering the Dharma solely to the Buddha, he intended that the future Buddha would personally receive the Patriarchal Dharma and subsequently propagate its transformation.
Bodhidharma said: "The inner transmission of the Dharma-seal serves to verify the mind through realization; the outer conferral of the *kāṣāya* robe serves to establish the fundamental tenet."
This is because the essential purpose lies in the robe; by means of the seal, one transmits the realization of one’s own mind.
Hereafter, as it will become difficult for people to arise [with such realization], I shall merely produce this robe and display the Dharma verses to manifest that my transformation is unimpeded.
This is because people may believe in the gate of self-awakening, yet fail to believe in the teacher's Dharma, thereby forgetting the mind of awakening and completion.
It is wondrous! Therefore, the robe is used to manifest this, so that people may awaken to it. Furthermore, awakening leads to the exhaustion of discriminative wisdom (*vibhāga-jñāna*).

When discrimination is exhausted, the fundamental delusions finally cease. As for the statement that after two hundred years following my parinirvāṇa, the robe will no longer be transmitted while the Dharma will pervade the entire realm of saṃsāra:
this is because those who have attained the Dharma through the realization of the mind are many; such realization must necessarily exhaust all phenomena before coming to rest.
It does not depend on representing each [point] individually with clothing. Regarding the statement that "those who clarify the Way are many, but those who practice the Way are few":

this refers to those who have attained self-awakening; they clarify only the path of the mind alone. Because they lack the skillful means to fully exhaust the wisdom of differentiation, they are unable to practice.

Regarding the statement that "those who explain the principle are many, but those who penetrate the principle are few": those who merely explain the principle have not awakened to the mind, but only transmit the Dharma.
This is so. One who has penetrated the principle is one who has attained realization in both their own mind and the fundamental teaching.
This is an exhortation that one must first attain the mind and then the Dharma before being able to practice; one must first attain the Dharma and then the mind before attaining actual realization.

These two cannot be lacking one another; therefore, one should secretly accord with and secretly realize the Dharma. There are more than ten million such instances of secret accordance and secret realization.
It is said that the World-Honored One entrusted [the teaching] before the Many-Sons Stūpa, saying, "Do not allow it to be severed.

Since the mind-dharma must certainly remain unbroken, there are more than ten million [beings who possess it]. You should propagate it; do not slight those who have not yet awakened. A single thought-moment of turning the mechanism is identical to original attainment.
This means that for people, regardless of whether their faculties are superior or inferior, they simply have not awakened. If one were shown this single thought-moment...
When the function returns, it is identical to what was originally attained. This mind that was originally attained accords with the Dharma; it is then non-dual with the patriarchs and Buddhas.
When those who transmit the Dharma and deliver the deluded masses speak of "transmission," they mean the Dharma; they do not mean there is a person who can be awakened to and transmitted.
That the Fifth Patriarch wrapped the Sixth Patriarch in his *kāṣāya* so that no one would see him while transmitting the Dharma was precisely at the Many Sons Stupa.
Regarding the preceding events: since the time of the Sixth Patriarch, everyone has known and believed in this Dharma-characteristic of "reality is formlessness.
All have said that the robe was used as a token of faith, precisely because they valued the existence of a core teaching (zongzhi). Alas! How can one not believe in the core teaching?
If one does not believe in the core teaching, what further use is there for the successive transmission from Buddha to Patriarch? What further use is there for the lineage of sources?
Names are merely designations. Thus, the five schools feared that their Dharma might perish; they manifested their fundamental tenets in words to transmit them.

After this transmission had continued for a long time, those who failed to awaken to the mind began to believe there was a dharma that could be passed on, and so they studied the teachings without integrating them with the mind.
Therefore, later "heroes" who have attained awakening desire to wipe away the fundamental tenets (*zongzhi*) and preserve only the view of awakening.

This is merely the fault of partiality arising from differing approaches to the Dharma of the mind. Herein, I provide a direct commentary on the Dharma of the mind transmitted by the Buddhas and Patriarchs, in order to demonstrate the principle that this Dharma of the mind is transmitted as a single lineage.
May future generations believe in it; then the prophecy of "many sons" will not prove false, and [the lineage] shall endure for thousands of myriads of years.

The words of others are finally proven true. If one insists on valuing self-awakening while brushing aside the teachings transmitted through tradition, they are certainly not a person who has awakened their mind.
Why is this? Because they perceive the existence of dharmas; to perceive the existence of dharmas is to contradict one's own mind.
Since they have awakened to the perception of existing dharmas, the mind that has awakened is likewise false. Alas! From oneself—
The Mind is the Teacher of the Dharma; it must not be moved or attached to. To move or attach to it is to enter hell as swiftly as a shot arrow.
*The Source of the Five Houses* (concludes).
Attached: Verses on the Words of the Ji School.
Wanfeng Fazang, a student of the Dharma, records:

While reading this, I exerted my own efforts to investigate within the sound of breaking bamboo. There, I attained the severance of the past and future limits and suddenly realized the essential meaning of the "Qingzhou Shirt.
Thus, I was able to see blood with every blow and hit the mark with every arrow. Furthermore, by investigating the Master Within Sleep, I fully comprehended the High [Patriarch].
Fengzhenluo, Xueyan, and Gubo shared a single heart across ten thousand ages; through this, one comes to know that the Way is without end.

By practicing with relentless vigor and closing oneself in retreat to investigate day and night that which cannot be investigated, one enters deeply into the inner sanctum of the Ji lineage and extends to the four houses, while also encompassing the various collateral branches of Chan.
Thus, one attains what Dahui called the wondrous state in which Chan embodies all its diverse forms.

The Three Mysteries and Three Essentials, the Four Aspects of Guest and Host, and the Great and Small Dharmas all derive from the Seven Buddhas’ Gāthā secretly transmitted by Bodhidharma to the Second Patriarch.

This essential Dharma of the Mind, passed down through the four and seven patriarchs of the Western Heaven, was transmitted until it reached the Sixth Patriarch, from whom it emerged through the two lineages of Nanyue and Qingyuan.
Thus, the great traditions of these two houses flourished, giving rise to such karmic conditions as Baizhang’s second visit to Mazu.
Taking all the aforementioned dharmas as the basis, Baizhang manifested his true character. For three days, Baizhang’s ears were deaf;
he transmitted this to Huangbo. Huangbo transmitted it through three blows of the staff to Linji.

Fearing that the essential teaching was too profound and might become distorted over time—transforming into a "one-sided" style of Zen that is coarse, vulgar, shallow, and trivial, sufficient only for one's own private realization but incapable of benefiting others—Linji [transmitted it further].
Therefore, together with Puhua, Ke Fu, and others, he established the fundamental tenets and their designations;

though these manifested in a thousand transformations and myriad changes, they were all gathered back into the "Two Halls" and the "Single Shout," divided into guest and host, and transmitted to San-sheng and Da-jue.

San-sheng and Da-jue summarized the indications and expanded upon them, mutually stimulating and exalting one another, and transmitted them to Xing-hua. Thus, the Dharma of the Patriarchs and Buddhas reached its ultimate perfection through Xing-hua.
Its subtlety is beyond words. At that time, those such as Lumén followed the echoes of empty sounds and nearly lost the fundamental tenets.
Fortunately, there was Shǒukòu who elucidated them for us; thus this Way relied on him not to perish. Subsequently, Dōushuài heard it from Qīngsù, and Juéfàn obtained it at Guīzōng.
Fearing that its profound essence might not be transmitted far, each of them expounded and propagated it. Such is the single lineage of Línjì.

The verses of the Seven Buddhas are fully preserved in the canonical records; this is precisely what is meant by saying that the literary and historical documents are sufficient, and I am able to verify them.
Later generations, however, encountered repeated turmoil during the times of Gao Feng and Zhongfeng, and among the various lineages of dharma-transmitting disciples during that interval...
Having served [his master] for no long time, his grasp of the fundamental tenets gradually grew distant.
By the beginning of our Ming dynasty, the teachings were but a flickering embers; yet, reaching the passes and ridges, they reached Xioyan. Among his disciples was Master Guangtong.
Failing to recognize the orthodox tradition from its own source, he recklessly attempted to fathom it with a small shell.

He then composed a preface to the *Xiaoyan ji* (Anthology of Xiyuan), asserting that beneath Caoxi, various divergent branches had spread out in all directions; that these possessed strange names and eccentric appearances, each maintaining its own boundaries to ensnare scholars throughout the realm;
and that because they falsely slandered their own masters, they had eliminated the Linji lineage, refusing to acknowledge its succession, and were thus pruning away the branches.

Tracing the current back to restore the original source, he gave it a new title: *The True Lineage of Caoxi*. Once this teaching was proclaimed, everyone rejoiced at its economy of effort and ease of understanding;
consequently, in recent years, those throughout the land who called themselves "good knowledge-holders" (shanzhishi) have... [fallen into decline].

They compete with one another in claiming that the annihilation of the fundamental tenets constitutes true awakening. Consequently, this leaves no means of restraint for those who are lawless, allowing them to recklessly adopt the ways of "chicken-crowing and dog-stealing" thieves;
they proclaim themselves kings and lords, beyond all possibility of verification. Truly, this is a case of borrowing something for a long time without ever returning it.
Alas! Is it then that Linji’s lineage has truly become a deviant branch? Is it that the fundamental tenets have truly become nothing more than strange names and eccentric forms?
Do they run wild and unrestrained? Is their Dharma truly intended to encompass the whole world? Are those who enter this Dharma truly like the deceptions of secret chamber transmissions?

Under Caoxi, were the lineages of Nanyue, Qingyuan, and the Five Houses all merely offshoots, yet now clamoring in confusion to claim the title of "Orthodox Lineage"? How is this any different from [the claims of] Guifeng?
Is it not for those who are merely superficial students to take Mount Nanyue as the pinnacle? Will there not be those with clear eyes in future generations who will laugh and reject such views?
Have you not heard the public case of Xigyan’s ascent to the hall, where he cited the precedent of the World-Honored One ascending the seat? At that time, a monk came forward and prostrated;
Xigyan struck him across the spine and said, "Why so talkative? The monk replied, "I have not yet uttered a single word; why do you call me talkative?"
Yan struck again, saying, "A second offense will not be tolerated. The following day, he ascended the hall and said: "Yesterday’s koan was not yet resolved;
I have not been able to dispel the delusions of you all, nor have I been able to walk hand-in-hand with the World-Honored One. Why is this so?
If one is a true connoisseur or a master of the Way, as soon as it is thus, it is not thus; only then is there no further connection. I shall simply let both ends fall away."
Open it. Let go in the midst; naturally, there will be a state of vivid, independent clarity. Taking charge wherever you are, it is like water merging with water, or space uniting with space.
Even Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot know it; ghosts and spirits cannot fathom it. Furthermore, a monk asked:

"What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'? Yankong said: "One copper coin. One fried cake. [The monk] asked: "What is 'taking away the environment but not taking away the person'?"
"Taking away from others. [The Master] said, "It has been eaten inside the belly; for the moment, one is full and joyful. [The Questioner] asked, "What is 'taking away both person and environment'?
[The Master] said, "You have not a single coin; you can only endure hunger. [The Questioner] asked, "What is 'neither taking away the person nor taking away the environment'?
[The Master] said, "Cloud Gate’s cakes and Golden Ox’s rice—coming with an empty stomach, returning with a full belly. Is this not so?"

Regarding the Linji lineage of Soran: having heard Soran’s words all day long and having read Soran’s records, to then establish a false argument to slander Soran as one who views Linji from the outside—is this not both excessive and erroneous?

Have you not heard the discourse on "preserving the sheep because of the love for the ritual," and the teaching that "one must not allow [the tradition] to be severed"? It is fortunate indeed that this single branch of Kimsul still remains and is thus employed.
Huangbo’s three severe blows of the staff were intended to instruct people; yet the Three Mysteries and the Host-Guest dynamics remain firmly established therein.
This unworthy one has striven to act as a successor and has vigorously proclaimed this school as an unchanging standard for ten thousand generations.

Alas, how it is that upon its proclamation, those who respond are few, such that it has not yet been able to expand and flourish to save the Zen lineage from the peril of extinction. I have thus respectfully examined the five schools, and—

Furthermore, I shall carefully recite the transmission records (gong'an) of the Mazu lineage for you to bestow upon two or three disciples who have attained self-awakening and entered the Way through their own realization.
Let us mutually stimulate and uplift one another, striving to cause this school to rise once more so that it does not perish, thereby repaying the Buddha's kindness.
If one were to say, "When Bodhidharma came from the West, there was originally not a single word; why then do you add these repetitive words? [it would be a grave error].
"Ya! He was about to respond, whereupon [the Master] said, "Do you take the verses of the Seven Buddhas and the various prophetic utterances to be mere words?
Thereupon, as soon as the other opened his mouth, he struck him with his palm, thereby severing the lineage of wild foxes for all future generations.
Citing Baizhang’s second visit to Mazu: While standing in attendance, Mazu looked at the whisk in the corner of his meditation seat.
Baizhang said, "Is it used right here, or apart from this? Mazu replied, "When you open your mouth in the future, what will you use to save people?
Baizhang picked up the whisk and held it upright. Mazu said, "Is it used right here, or apart from this? Baizhang then hung the whisk back on its stand.
At his former residence, Mazu let out a single shout that caused Baizhang to go deaf for three days. Not long after, he resided at Mount Daxiong;
because the surrounding cliffs and peaks were so steep and lofty, it was named Baizhang (Hundred Fathoms). Scholars from all quarters flocked there like deer.
One day he said to the assembly, "The Buddha-dharma is no small matter.
In the past, when I was struck by Mazu’s single shout, my ears were deaf for three days. When Huangbo heard this being mentioned, he involuntarily stuck out his tongue.
Linji said, "Will you not take Mazu as your successor in the future? Huangbo replied, "Not so. Today, because the Master mentioned it, I have attained [realization]."
He saw Mazu’s great function of spiritual power, yet he did not recognize Mazu. [Huineng] said, "If you succeed Mazu, your descendants will later lose their own selves.
Baizhang said, "So it is, so it is. When one's insight is equal to the teacher, one lacks half the teacher's virtue;
only when one's insight surpasses the teacher is one fit for transmission. You possess a vision that greatly transcends your teacher. Baizhang then prostrated himself. Furthermore—
Yangshan said, "This reveals great capacity and great function. But tell me, what is the function of great capacity?
He added the comment: "A flash of lightning before the saddle; a clap of thunder behind the horse. He further said, "When spring winds have passed, there are summer rains."
The verse says:
It is said that the heroic will may be fulfilled; Rushing forward and sweeping all before him, his spirit is revealed. The gourd-valley is severed, the fire reaches the heavens;
How many can become dragons from a single horse?
"What is the great capacity and great function? The commentary says: "Three surges at the Dragon Gate;
a clap of thunder on level ground.
The verse says:
Sending forth and drawing back, it acts with total freedom; suddenly it turns its tail and head upside down.
Having once faced the perils of the Three Gorges and Qutang Pass, even the little child who leaps over the hearth was filled with great anxiety.
Since there is already the function of the great capacity, what then is the capacity for that great function? The commentary says:
"If not led by the fisherman, how could one see the waves?"
The verse says:
Bowl beneath, the kāṣāya over the body in the cave; A hero displaying his prowess as a general on that day. After leaving Mount Meng, the Southern School flourished;
Avoiding the stone, he still transmits his merit for ten thousand ages.
"What is the great principle? The commentary says: "The large fruit is not eaten. The verse says:
"Crossing waters and traversing mountains without weariness; when the peach blossoms have flowed away, one beholds the source of the immortals. Since falling once among the fishermen..."

Regarding the "Eye": there is a worldly tradition of idle talk claiming that the dialogue between guest and host already existed from the time of Mazu downward. Its source, however, actually derives from the "Bai Zhang’s Second Visit" public case.
Now tell me: what is the "host within the guest" of Bai Zhang’s second visit? The commentary states:
When Zhou Lang’s merit was achieved, Han possessed Jingzhou.
The eulogy says:

"Early on he applied the simplified laws, next [conquered] Guanzhong; showing the jade ring, he boiled the old man; his hegemony was truly heroic. At midnight came the Chu songs within the bedchamber of Yu."
Cold. For a thousand autumns, there has been no face seen in Jiangdong.
What is the guest within the host? The verbal response says: "The night before the summer solstice is already settled.
The verse says:

First bowing at the eastern steps, he expresses his utmost courtesy; facing north, he lifts the cup with frequent gestures of ritual deference. Only when pride and excess have been cast away can one see the true reality;
from the beginning, entry into sagehood has always been rooted in benevolence.
"What is the Lord of Lords? The verbal response says: "After the rain has passed, the thunder roars.
The verse says:
"Where does the sound of the wooden mallet strike and shatter the autumn? It overturns the light skiff and casts out the fishhook. The night moon knows not the depth of the lake."
Cold. It sinks to the very bottom of the Dragon Nest.
From where does the Master of Masters obtain it? The comment says: "Even if one has many patrons.
The verse says:
Leaning back beyond the threshold, he entrusts affairs to his generals; founding a state and establishing a family—how could these be the work of another?
It is not through the nobility of merely draping robes and folding hands that the myriad nations are able to come as guests.
